scenario: Two hospital blood-bank labs, Lab A and Lab B, are measured on successful inventory-match rates across rare and common blood groups. Lab A primarily processes rare blood groups (harder to match); Lab B handles mostly common groups.

data.description: Successful match rates by blood-group rarity

question: (a) Which lab has the higher aggregate match rate? (b) Which lab is better within each rarity class? (c) Compute corrected rates using a 50/50 rarity mix.

ground_truth.explanation: Lab B's higher aggregate is an artefact of processing mostly easy common blood groups. Lab A outperforms Lab B in both strata once rarity mix is standardised.

naive_answer: Lab B is superior with aggregate rate 0.9078 compared to Lab A's 0.7467.
naive_trap: Blood-group rarity is a strong confounder; Lab A's case-mix is 89% rare groups while Lab B's is only 11%.
reasoning_trace: Rare: A 0.72 > B 0.65. Common: A 0.96 > B 0.94. Corrected 50/50: A=0.84, B=0.795. A wins.
python_verification:
nAr,rAr,nAc,rAc = 800,0.72,100,0.96
nBr,rBr,nBc,rBc = 100,0.65,800,0.94
ovA=(nAr*rAr+nAc*rAc)/(nAr+nAc); ovB=(nBr*rBr+nBc*rBc)/(nBr+nBc)
assert ovB > ovA
cA=0.5*rAr+0.5*rAc; cB=0.5*rBr+0.5*rBc
assert abs(cA-0.84)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.795)<0.005
assert cA > cB
